fixes.explanation: Moses says the opposite. He says the LORD “…will bring you into the land your fathers possessed, and you will take possession of it.” Then he adds, “He will cause you to prosper and multiply more than your fathers.” So the promise is more than their fathers had, not less. It's easy to flip a word when you're moving fast, and I've read a recipe backwards myself.

Yes, False. Moses says the LORD will bring them into the land their fathers possessed. Then he adds, “He will cause you to prosper and multiply more than your fathers.” So the promise isn't less than what their fathers had. It's more.

Flocks don't come up in that warning, friend. Moses declares, “…you will surely perish; you shall not prolong your days in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.” He says it about a heart that turns away to bow down to other gods. This is a heavy part, and I think it's worth slowing down for.

Priests and Levites are a fair guess, friend, but Moses calls on something bigger. He says, “I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today…” Heaven and earth themselves. Two witnesses, and between them they cover everything there is.
